Knowledge of business and commercial law, including the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) and contract law, as they pertain to credit unions.

Knowledge of generally accepted industry standards and protocols for due diligence; including internal controls, control structure/environment, director and management accountability, fiduciary responsibility, reporting structures, and management oversight.
Knowledge of relevant economic issues, financial markets, and financial institutions.
Knowledge of tools and techniques (e.g., demographics, data aggregation, penetration, member relationship management) for promoting products, services, and programs.

Knowledge of credit union organizational structures (e.g., accountability, communication channels, work flow, delineation of responsibility, supervisory relationships, organizational chart) and general legal structures (e.g., CUSOs).
Knowledge of methods and tools used for enterprise-wide risk management (i.e. integrating assessments of risk across the credit union to determine and mitigate overall risk exposure).
Knowledge of statistical principles, methods, and tools; ability to use statistical data in order to make recommendations or decisions.

Knowledge of the fundamental aspects of the planning process.  Ability to analyze relationships between strategic and business plans and their impact on the credit union’s financial condition, operations, or reputation.
Ability to determine and prioritize areas to be reviewed during an examination or supervision contact.

Knowledge of lending principles, industry practices, and markets; including policies, underwriting and documentation, pricing, purchasing, selling, servicing, and collecting consumer, real estate, commercial loans, and participation loans.
Knowledge of examination procedures; ability to analyze information to identify and determine appropriate actions needed to resolve concerns.

Knowledge of the fundamentals of business finance, financial analysis, and asset-liability management (ALM) including internal and external sources of funding; ability to analyze and interpret financial trends and ratios, assess current financial conditions and projections.

Knowledge of the structure of electronic processing systems, information security, third party reviews, and disaster recovery, including electronic payment systems (e.g., web-based FedLine, electronic data processing (EDP), Internet).

Knowledge of federal, state, and local laws and regulations affecting credit unions (e.g., Federal Credit Union Act, NCUA Rules and Regulations, Bank Secrecy Act, Bylaws, consumer compliance regulations).

Knowledge of financial reporting, accounting theory and concepts covered by generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), with an emphasis on financial institutions; knowledge of accounting systems, structures, and controls; ability to evaluate financial statements and other financial records.

Knowledge of generally accepted auditing standards (GAAS) and procedures for financial and compliance audits; ability to understand the concepts of internal controls, substantive testing, and the auditor's report.

Knowledge of internal control structure and components that maintain integrity of financial and compliance reporting activities; ability to evaluate the credit union’s risk of material misstatement and compliace violations due to internal control deficiencies.
Knowledge of types of fraud, indicators of possible fraud, and techniques to identify, investigate, and document fraud.
Maintains and builds on policy knowledge to stay abreast of changes and updates to internal Agency policy and relevant external policies.

Knowledge of methods and tools used for credit risk management; ability to assess risk across the loan portfolio , including credit risk management practices and processes, allowance methodologies, collections, and workouts; ability to identify and evaluate mitigants for aggregate portfolio risk.

Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, industry practices, and markets related to business loans; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with individual business loans and the aggregate portfolio.

Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, and industry practices related to residential mortgage loans; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with mortgage loans.

Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, and industry practices related to indirect loans/leases; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with indirect loans/leases.

Knowledge of investment policies and principles, industry practices, and markets, including pre-purchase analysis, portfolio management, permissible investment activities, characteristics (e.g., cash flows, indices, pricing, optionality), and related risk.

Knowledge of regulations and supervisory guidance related to liquidity risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control liquidity risk; ability to assess liquidity risk, including actions to mitigate liquidity risk.

Knowledge of regulations and supervisory guidance related to interest rate risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control interest rate risk; ability to assess interest rate risk, including actions to mitigate interest rate risk.
Knowledge of models used to estimate the financial risks to which the institution is exposed; ability to assess adequacy of the credit union’s asset liability management (ALM) models and practices.

Knowledge of the laws, regulations, and supervisory guidance related to compliance risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control compliance risk; ability to assess compliance risk, including actions to mitigate compliance risk; ability to facilitate resolution when violations occur.

CompetencyName: Federal Consumer Protection Laws and Regulations
Description: Knowledge of federal consumer protection laws and regulations applicable to credit unions (for example, Truth in Savings Act, Regulations B, C, D, E, M, P, X, Z), including consequences of non-compliance; ability to determine compliance with laws and regulations.
Knowledge of payment system delivery channels, components, and structure; ability to assess payment systems and related risk, including actions to mitigate risk.
Knowledge of standards, processes, and practices to identify, measure, prevent, and mitigate risks, threats, and vulnerabilities associated with payment systems.

Knowledge of NCUA Rules and Regulations, agency directives and guidance, and  industry rules, guidelines, and best practices related to identifying, measuring, managing, monitoring, reporting, and controlling risks in payment systems; ability to assess governance and related risks.
Knowledge of logical and physical access controls and oversight activities used to ensure protection of credit union assets and integrity of payment information (e.g., member information, PII).

Knowledge of NCUA rules and regulations (e.g., RR Part 748, 749), agency directives and guidance, and industry best practices related to managing, monitoring, reporting, and controlling risks in information technology; ability to assess governance and related risks.

Knowledge of standards, tools, and practices to identify, detect, prevent, and mitigate information technology risks, threats, and vulnerabilities; includes the risk assessment process, risk management program, and the audit function; ability to assess adequacy of controls.
Knowledge of logical and physical tools and techniques to ensure protection, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and information.
Knowledge of policies, procedures, and practices (e.g., business impact analysis, risk management, testing) to ensure continuity of business operations in the event of a disaster or incident.

Knowledge of BSA/AML laws, rules, regulations, and supervisory guidance and the methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control BSA/AML compliance risk; ability to assess BSA/AML compliance risk and facilitate resolution when violations or deficiencies are identified.

CompetencyName: Office of Foreign Assets Control Compliance Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of OFAC laws, rules, regulations, and supervisory guidance and the methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control OFAC compliance risk; ability to assess OFAC compliance risk and facilitate resolution when violations or deficiencies are identified.
